preamble: The affrication of an aspirated alveolar stop [tʰ] to a postalveolar affricate [tʃ]. The documented case is the English syllable-onset cluster /tr/: the aspirated /t/ coarticulates with the following postalveolar approximant, so that tree sounds like 'chree' and truck like 'chruck'. Magloughlin (2018) shows that this coarticulatory effect is being phonologized in North American English. Speakers with a strongly retroflex /r/ produce a retroflex-like variant (see t_aspirated_to_ch_retroflex). The unaspirated /t/ after /s/ (street) and the /tj/ coalescence of tune are separate processes and are not included here.

examples.note: Onset /tr/ affricates through coarticulation with the postalveolar approximant; heterosyllabic /t.r/ (rat-race) does not.
The same onset affrication; children's spellings such as 'chruck' reflect it.
